We do not know how to prove they exist unconditionally (this would be a major breakthrough in complexity theory), so we must conjecture or assume their existence. Such a conjecture is based on the fact that several natural computational problems have received much attention, yet still have no polynomial-time algorithm for solving them. Perhaps the most famous such problem is integer factorization, i.e., finding the prime factors of a large integer. It is easy to multiply two numbers and obtain their product, but difficult to take a number and find its factors. This leads us to define the function fmult (x, y) = x · y.
